chunks: My father narrated (may God be pleased with him) who said: Ali ibn al-Hussein al-Sa'd Abadi narrated to me, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah al-Barqi, from Isma'il ibn Mihran, from Durost ibn Abi Mansur, from Isa ibn Bashir, from Abu Hamza al-Thumali, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

When death approached Ali ibn al-Hussein (peace be upon him), he hugged me to his chest and said: 'O my son, I advise you with what my father advised me when death approached him, and what he mentioned that his father had advised him with. O my son, beware of oppressing anyone who has no helper but God.'
ai.seo_question: What is the key ethical advice regarding oppression passed down through the Ahl al-Bayt?
ai.summary: This hadith, recorded in Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Al-Khisal*, highlights the transmission of ethical wisdom through the Ahl al-Bayt, specifically from Imam al-Baqir to his son, Imam Ali al-Zayn al-Abidin. The advice to avoid oppressing those who lack a human defender (*ghayr Allah*) underscores the Shia concept of divine justice (*Adl*) and the believer's role as God's vicegerent in maintaining social equity. It serves as a practical guide for personal conduct, reminding believers that ultimate accountability lies with God, who is the true protector of the oppressed.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 1-59 (The compiler of the book narrated) that his father - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Ali ibn al-Hussein al-Sa’ed Abady quoted on the authority of Ahmad ibn Aba Abdullah al-Barqy, on the authority of Isma’il ibn Mihran, on the authority of Durost ibn Abi Mansoor, on the authority of Isa ibn Bashir, on the authority of Abi Hamzih al-Sumaly that Abi Ja’far al-Baqir (MGB) said,

“When the time of death of the Blessed Ali ibn al-Hussein (MGB) arrived, he hugged me tightly and said, ‘O my son! I advise you to do what my father advised me to do at the time of his death, and reminded me what his father had advised him to do at the time of his death. O my son! I advise you not to oppress anyone who has no helper but God.’”
